issues.description: validate_conda has no stated precondition or postcondition and confuses 'looks plausible' with 'is a working conda executable'
issues.detail: The docstring claims the function checks the file 'is executable, and that calling it with --version identifies it as conda, mamba, or micromamba'. The postcondition is undefined: the function returns True for the empty string (which is not an executable at all), and it returns True whenever the substring 'conda', 'mamba', or 'micromamba' appears anywhere in stdout-lowercased. A path whose --version output merely mentions any of those words (a wrapper, a help banner, an unrelated tool that prints 'no mamba detected') will pass. No precondition is stated for conda_executable (type? trusted? user-supplied path that will be executed). Reason about what this predicate is supposed to mean before writing it; right now it is a fuzzy match dressed as validation.

issues.description: Smuggled control flow: validate_conda mixes early-return and a 'valid' flag, with inconsistent exception handling
issues.detail: Within one short function the author uses three different exit disciplines: an early `return True` on empty string, two early `return False` guards, a mutable `valid` flag set inside a try, and a `return False` in the except. The except swallows every Exception and treats it as 'not valid', while a subsequent unrelated exception path (e.g. UnicodeDecodeError on `out.decode()`) is also silently 'not valid'. This is the structured-programming smell Dijkstra would name: the control flow is not a clean sequence/selection over a stated invariant, it is an ad-hoc flag braided with returns. Either reason the predicate as a single Boolean expression over guarded subchecks, or state the invariant the `valid` flag is supposed to maintain. As written, a reader must simulate the function to know what it returns.

issues.description: Executing a user-supplied path inside a 'validation' predicate has no stated frame and unbounded side effects
issues.detail: validate_conda invokes `run_program(conda_executable, ['--version'])` on whatever path the user typed into a preferences textbox. The frame is unstated: this predicate spawns a process, may hang (no timeout on .communicate()), may produce stderr output, and on Windows will happily execute an arbitrary .exe the user pointed at. A function named 'validate' is expected to be a pure predicate over the argument; this one has effects on the operating system. State the precondition (path is trusted to the same degree as PATH entries), document that this executes the file, and add a timeout to .communicate() so a misbehaving binary cannot wedge the preferences dialog.

issues.description: Windows-only `*.exe` filter excludes the very cases the feature was added to support
issues.detail: The confpage uses `filters='*.exe'` on the conda browse field. On Linux and macOS the conda/mamba/micromamba executables have no extension; the file dialog will hide them. The feature exists precisely because users have conda installed in 'non-standard locations' — and on Unix the standard location yields an extensionless binary. State the precondition for the filter or remove it. As written, the dialog is wrong on the majority of platforms Spyder runs on.

issues.description: kernelspec.argv silently falls back when custom_conda is enabled but conda_path is empty; the postcondition of the branch is unstated
issues.detail: The new logic reads: if find_conda() failed, then if `custom_conda` is set use `conda_path`, else None; then if still falsy, raise. There is no check that when `custom_conda` is True the user-supplied `conda_path` is non-empty and points to an existing executable. The earlier validate_conda runs in the preferences dialog but does not gate config persistence — the stored value may be empty, stale, or pointing at a deleted file. State the postcondition of this block ('on exit, conda_exe is a path to an executable that responds to --version as conda/mamba/micromamba') and enforce it here rather than trusting the preferences dialog to have done so.

issues.description: Decision to override find_conda() only when it fails is an undocumented policy, not a reasoned spec
issues.detail: The new code only consults the user's custom conda when `find_conda()` returns falsy. That means a user who explicitly set a custom Conda executable because the auto-detected one is wrong will be silently ignored whenever auto-detection succeeds. The user-facing checkbox is labeled 'Use a custom Conda/Mamba/Micromamba executable' and the tooltip says 'Use the specified Conda… instead of finding the executable from the interpreter path' — but the code does the opposite ordering. Either the spec is 'custom overrides auto' (then check custom_conda first) or 'custom is a fallback' (then change the UI text). State which, then write the code to match.

issues.description: create_browsefile gains validate_callback / validate_reason parameters with no documented contract
issues.detail: The signature is extended with two new keyword arguments that are forwarded into create_lineedit, but neither the docstring (there isn't one) nor a type indicates: when is the callback invoked, with what argument, what return type, and what is validate_reason used for. A library function whose contract is 'read the call sites to find out' is exactly the kind of accreted complexity that defeats local reasoning. State the precondition and postcondition of the callback in a docstring.

issues.description: Unrelated change: select_file now steals focus back to the edit after a file is chosen
issues.detail: The diff adds `edit.setFocus()` inside select_file with no mention in the PR description. This affects every consumer of create_browsefile across Spyder, not just the new conda field. Side changes whose frame is 'the whole application' should not be smuggled into a feature PR; if it is needed for the conda field, do it at that call site or justify it for all call sites.

issues.description: No tests accompany the new validation predicate or the kernelspec fallback branch
issues.detail: The PR adds a new config key, a new public utility (`validate_conda`), and a new branch in kernelspec.argv. The author offers no evidence of correctness beyond a screenshot. Testing shows the presence of bugs, not their absence — but here we do not even have that. At minimum: unit tests for validate_conda covering empty string, nonexistent path, non-executable file, executable that prints an unrelated --version, and an executable that prints 'conda 24.1.2'; and a test that the kernelspec branch raises the correct SpyderKernelError when custom_conda is True but conda_path is empty.

review.summary: The feature solves a real user need but the code has not been reasoned about before being written. validate_conda is a fuzzy substring match dressed as a validation predicate, with smuggled control flow (early returns braided with a flag), a swallowed bare-Exception catch, and no stated pre/postcondition; it also executes a user-supplied path with no timeout. The new kernelspec branch and the preferences UI disagree about whether 'custom conda' is an override or a fallback, and the .exe-only file filter is wrong on the platforms where the feature is most needed. No tests, no docstrings stating contracts; the evidence offered is a screenshot. TESTED-NOT-PROVED at best, UNREASONED in the validation predicate. Verdict: REFUSED in its current form — accept the design intent, but require a stated specification for validate_conda, a stated precedence rule for custom-vs-auto, a cross-platform file filter, and tests before merge.
